---
title: "Claude at the School of Medicine"
subtitle: "Training materials from the Yale Cushing/Whitney Medical Library"
---

These pages are the class materials for two in-person classes from the Cushing/Whitney Medical Library. **Getting started with Claude** shows anyone at the School of Medicine how to use the Claude app well and safely. **Analyzing research data with Claude Code** teaches researchers to clean and analyze study data. The second class builds on the first, but you can take either one on its own. Instructors teach from these pages, so you can follow along in class or work through them on your own.

## What you'll learn {#learn}

### Getting started with Claude

1. Identify the right tool and settings for your data.
2. Apply prompting patterns to a real task.
3. Evaluate Claude's answers and citations before you use them.
4. Create a Project you can reuse for your own work.

### Analyzing research data with Claude Code

1. **Configure** a Claude Code project that protects raw and restricted data.
2. **Implement** a plan-first workflow to clean and analyze study data.
3. **Distinguish** tasks to delegate to Claude from decisions you keep.
4. **Evaluate** AI-generated code and results against the analysis plan.

## The two classes {#classes}

| | Getting started with Claude | Analyzing research data with Claude Code |
|---|---|---|
| **For** | Anyone at the School of Medicine. No programming needed. | Researchers, coordinators, analysts, and clinicians who can read a little R. *Getting started with Claude* helps but isn't required. |
| **What you'll do** | Build a Claude Project you'll keep using, then prompt it well and check what it gives you. | Use Claude Code in Positron to prepare and analyze real CDC survey data (NHANES) and reproduce a published CDC estimate. You make the decisions and check every step. |
| **Time** | 60 minutes | 90 minutes |
| **Where** | In person, SHM L 111, up to 18 people | In person, SHM L 111, up to 18 people |

## Data use {#data}

::: {.callout-warning title="No patient data, ever"}
- In class, use **only the class files and public information**. Never use patient data or other sensitive information in either class.
- **A HIPAA-supported version of Claude is available by request** (see the [ITS service page for Claude Enterprise](https://yale.service-now.com/it?id=service_offering&sys_id=f6429096337382106bab02b19e5c7bf4)). Being HIPAA-supported doesn't approve your project, every feature, or every data set.
- Before you use Claude with real work data, follow [Yale's data classification](https://cybersecurity.yale.edu/data-classification). Questions go to `[HSIT / HIPAA Privacy Office contact]`.
:::

Both classes use only fictional (synthetic) files or public, openly licensed material. The article in *Getting started with Claude* is an open-access paper (Hickey et al., *PLoS Medicine* 2025, CC BY). *Analyzing research data with Claude Code* uses real, public CDC survey data (NHANES, August 2021–August 2023). It's de-identified survey data, not patient data. The NCHS data user agreement still applies: use it for statistical analysis only, never try to identify anyone, and never link it to other data about the same people.

## Setup for Getting started with Claude {#setup-part1}

### 1. Download Claude app

- [ ] Download and install the [**Claude** desktop app](https://claude.ai/downloads).
- [ ] In a web browser, go to [**claude.ai**](https://claude.ai), sign in with your Yale account, and send a test message such as "Hello."


### 2. Choose your practice kit

In class you'll build a Claude **Project**: a workspace with your own instructions and files. Pick one kit. Both use the same steps.

| Kit | Who it's for | What's in it | Download |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kit A: Article Explainer** (default) | Anyone who reads or explains research articles | A style guide (fictional) and a text copy of an open-access article (Hickey et al., *PLoS Medicine* 2025, CC BY) | [part1-kit-a.zip](downloads/part1-kit-a.zip) |
| **Kit B: Committee Assistant** | Administrative staff who run meetings and committees | A made-up committee charter and meeting notes | [part1-kit-b.zip](downloads/part1-kit-b.zip) |

- [ ] Download your kit's zip file and unzip it somewhere easy to find, such as `Documents`. On Windows, right-click the zip and choose **Extract All**.
- [ ] **Don't upload anything yet.** In class, we'll check your settings first, then build the Project together.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Individual files, and the Windows .md.txt problem"}
**Individual files** (if you'd rather not use a zip):

- Kit A: [explainer-style-guide.md](materials/part1-kits/kit-a/explainer-style-guide.md) · [hickey-2025-telehealth-htn.md](materials/part1-kits/kit-a/hickey-2025-telehealth-htn.md)
- Kit B: [committee-pack-synthetic.md](materials/part1-kits/kit-b/committee-pack-synthetic.md)
- About the kits: [README.md](materials/part1-kits/README.md)

To save a single file, right-click the link and choose **Save link as** (or **Download linked file**). If you just click it, the file may open as text in your browser.

**Windows:** your file may save as `name.md.txt`. That's fine; Claude can read it. To fix the name, open File Explorer, choose **View > Show > File name extensions**, and delete `.txt` from the end.
:::

### 3. Optional: the Claude phone app

Near the end of class we'll open your Project on a phone. This step is optional; you can do everything on your laptop.

- [ ] Install **Claude** from the App Store (iPhone) or Google Play (Android). Check that the publisher is **Anthropic**.
- [ ] Sign in with the same Yale account.
- [ ] Never photograph patient lists, charts, screens, or whiteboards. If you use the HIPAA-supported version, check with [Health Sciences IT](https://healthsciencesit.yale.edu/) before using the phone app.

## Setup for Analyzing research data with Claude Code {#setup-part2}

About 30 minutes. Do the steps in order. You need a Yale Claude account whose seat includes **Claude Code**.

### 1. Positron and R

[Positron](https://positron.posit.co) is a free data science editor from Posit, the makers of RStudio. It works with R and supports Quarto. VS Code (version 1.94 or later) works too, but class is taught in Positron.

- [ ] Install Positron: <https://positron.posit.co/download.html>
- [ ] Install **R** from <https://cloud.r-project.org>. Positron should find R. If it doesn't, restart Positron, then ask the instructors.
- [ ] In Positron's **Console**, install the class packages:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "haven", "survey", "here", "gtsummary", "gt", "broom", "janitor", "testthat"))
```

The class uses R only. If you work in Python, pair with an R user or follow along.

### 2. git (required)

In class, git saves checkpoints of your work so you can undo mistakes.

- [ ] **macOS:** open **Terminal** and run `xcode-select --install`. This installs Apple's Command Line Tools, which include git. If it says they're already installed, you're done.
- [ ] **Windows:** install **Git for Windows** from <https://git-scm.com/downloads>. Accept the default options.
- [ ] Set your name and email. In Positron, open the **Terminal** tab and run:

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@yale.edu"
```

### 3. The Claude Code extension

- [ ] In Positron, open the **Extensions** view from the Activity Bar on the left.
- [ ] Search for **Claude Code** and install the extension published by **Anthropic**. (Positron installs extensions from a mirror of the Open VSX catalog; VS Code uses its own marketplace.)
- [ ] Open the Claude Code panel and sign in with your Yale Claude account.

### 4. The practice project

- [ ] Download [nhanes-bp.zip](downloads/nhanes-bp.zip). It holds three real data files from the CDC's National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), August 2021–August 2023: demographics, blood pressure readings, and a blood pressure questionnaire. It also has the CDC codebooks, a data dictionary, and a one-page analysis plan.
- [ ] Unzip it somewhere easy to find, such as `Documents`. On Windows, right-click the zip and choose **Extract All**. If you end up with an `nhanes-bp` folder inside another `nhanes-bp` folder, use the inner one.
- [ ] In Positron, choose **File > Open Folder** and select the `nhanes-bp` folder.

### 5. Check that it works

- [ ] In the Claude Code panel, send this prompt:

```text
Read the README and CLAUDE.md, then tell me in three sentences what this project is.
```

If Claude describes CDC NHANES blood-pressure data from 2021–2023, you're ready.

- [ ] Check that Claude can run R and git for you. Send this prompt. If Claude asks to run a command, allow it:

```text
Run `Rscript --version` and `git --version`, then tell me what each one printed.
```

If both print a version number, Claude can run R and git. If one fails, check that it's installed, restart Positron, and try again.

**Windows:** the R installer doesn't add `Rscript` to your PATH, so Claude can't find it. Open Start, search for **Edit environment variables for your account**, select **Path**, click **Edit**, then **New**, and add R's `bin` folder, usually `C:\Program Files\R\R-4.x.x\bin` (use your version's folder). Click OK, restart Positron, and run the prompt again.

- [ ] Type `/status` in the panel. Check that it shows your Yale account. Note the version number.

## Access and alternatives {#access}

| If… | Do this |
|---|---|
| **You don't have a working Claude account** | See [Claude @ Yale](https://ai.yale.edu/yales-ai-tools-and-resources/claude) for an overview, then [request a Claude account](https://yale.service-now.com/it?id=service_offering&sys_id=f6429096337382106bab02b19e5c7bf4) before class. In class, pair up with someone who has one. In *Getting started with Claude*, you can also follow along in [Clarity](https://clarity.yale.edu) where it has the same feature. You can also use a free Claude account, but don't put any Yale information in it: use it only for the public class files. |
